chapters.title: Chapter 3799: A Quintessential Place! II
paragraphs: The air within the Living Origin Labyrinth shimmered, thick with potential.
Before Noah’s eyes, more Prompts unfolded in delicate succession, each one branded in elegant golden runes visible only to him, but mirrored in different ways to everyone present.
|In the Living Origin Labyrinth, nothing within is affected by any type of authority except a unique Living Origin Authority.|

|Before you are 81 Living Origin Starter Cubes. Coming in contact with one will grant you an identity and distinction of a varying type of a Living Origin Garden Archetype. Through your Archetype, you can exert control and influence your surroundings.|

|Once you have attained a Living Origin Garden Archetype, its growth is purely dependent on Resistance Archetype Points which are innately obtained based on how much True Absolute Existential Resistance one has, or Resistance Archetype Points obtained from challenges of the Living Origin Labyrinth, or those obtained from Unique Sources within the Living Origin Labyrinth.|

|You currently hold 200 Resistance Archetype Points to distribute to your Living Origin Garden Archetype once it has been selected. 100 Points stem from your Resistance Percentages, and 100 Points stem from the achievement of being the holder of the Living Origin Key.|
The information settled around him like dust in sunlight, luminous and silent.
Noah’s mind processed it instantly as his eyes were shining with a terrifying light!
Everything in here... is disconnected from authority unless it’s Living Origin Authority.
That changed the playing field entirely.
A self-contained domain.
One that leveled the battlefield by stripping traditional advantages and replacing them with a new kind of distinction: Archetypes.
Eighty-one of them.
And only one per person.
They weren’t just tools. They were identities within this Labyrinth. Interfaces of control and evolution.
Then came the second revelation.
Resistance Archetype Points.
The Role of True Absolute Existential Resistances. A point that meant those who were extremely powerful would remain extremely powerful...initially at least.
The Resistances weren’t just defenses here, they were keys in and of themselves. Each Resistance type translated into influence over the power one could display here!
And he had 200 to start with.
One hundred from his rare feat of 10% in all ten Resistances. And another hundred for being the Holder of the Living Origin Key.
His eyes drifted across the room.
Everyone else had received similar information, though the points they began with likely varied.
Master Shen. Master Hannibal.
He looked at them briefly, curiosity threading through his thoughts.
They both carried multiple Resistances- likely unique to their tier. But they didn’t have ten like he did. Nobody else did.
The question struck him then.
What changes when one becomes an Originus Venerant that allows them to hold multiple True Absolute Existential Resistances... from a single True Source?
It was an ascension past Primarchy. A transition that let even one True Source branch out into multiple Resistances, increasing flexibility and power exponentially.
It was something to study and understand.
But still... even they were limited by what their Sources could provide.
He, however, had ten distinct True Sources.
Ten Resistance paths.

If his starting point was 200, he guessed that high-tier Primarchs would have between 10 to 99 Resistance Archetype Points, depending on their alignment with Resistances as even the most powerful Primarchs held 95% or 99% Origin or Conceptual Resistance within the Veield Sunfolds.
But Shen? Hannibal?
400, maybe 500 points since they held multiple Resistances!
Their Archetypes would be monstrous.
But...
This was the Living Origin Labyrinth.
And there was a lot that was still unknown!
Noah’s gaze flicked toward the periphery.
The space they stood in was one of three defined zones in this crimson-gold domain.
Zone One- The gathering space. Where they had all been deposited.
Zone Two- The middle ground, occupied by the fifty towering humanoid golems with blank white masks- sentinels of unknown origin and purpose.
Zone Three: The distant wall where nine massive chests sat like silent monarchs, glowing with an intensity that made even Masters of Existence pause.
They were sealed.
Untouched.
Waiting.
Noah’s grip on the golden tether tightened slightly as Sigrid, wide-eyed, pulled gently on it.
She tilted her head toward him and signed with urgency and wonder.
[Woah, did you also see the words that flashed before me? Living Origin Garden Archetype? Resistance Points? Is this normal???]
Noah let out a soft chuckle, his tone dry. "It’s unique, but not that crazy."
She stared at him, unconvinced.
From the side, Master Shen laughed as he downed another swig from his gourd and gestured lazily toward the front.
"Alright," he said, "I’m guessing you all saw the same weavings as us."
He pointed to three Primarchs nearby- a man wreathed in stormlight, a violet-robed woman with green crystalline eyes, and another cloaked in starlight.

"You three. Let’s have you be our lab rats. Step up and pick a cube. Let’s see what the Labyrinth gives you. Because all of this...is entirely different to what the Origin Wonder normally led to. We have to take it a step at a time."
The three nodded, stepping forward without hesitation.
Their feet touched the crimson-gold stone with grace and purpose.
Noah’s gaze followed them closely.
Then it drifted to the Living Origin Starter Cubes for the first time.
Each one hovered in the air at shoulder height, crimson-gold polyhedrons that emitted soft light in rhythmic pulses.
They weren’t just glowing geometric artifacts.
Their surfaces bore a triangular runic marking eerily similar to the one on Sigrid’s forehead.
But there was more.
Inside each triangle were intricate symbols. Layers upon layers of swirling runes written in ancient tongues that even Noah’s perceptive mind could barely begin to decipher.
Some symbols glowed blue, others green, others the color of molten silver.
The scripts danced and changed as if reading the soul of anyone who looked upon them.
No two were the same.
Each Starter Cube was alive in its own way- waiting to be chosen!
And Noah?
He watched with silent interest, the beginnings of a plan already forming as he observed the three Primarchs going forward!

chapters.title: Chapter 3800: A Quintessential Place! III
paragraphs: The first of the Primarchs stepped forward.

A lithe woman with a crown of coiling hair touched one of the floating crimson-gold cubes- specifically, a cube with a rune marker that never remained still. It flickered like a snake on glass, its runic triangle constantly shifting.
And for a flicker of a moment, Noah’s eyes narrowed as he parsed the meaning.
Cold.
Something buried beneath the surface of frost. Of stillness. Of ancient glacial ruin.
Or so he believed from what he could decipher.
The moment the Primarch’s hand met the cube, it pulsed.
BOOM!
The crimson-gold light exploded into her chest like a heartbeat made of ice and radiance. She stumbled a step, then steadied herself with wide eyes.
Noah caught the expression. Euphoria. Surprise.
The other two Primarchs moved quickly.
Each chose a cube and touched it, their selections less chaotic, more instinctive.
Light streamed from the cubes, curling into their chests with sharp flashes.
One breathed in deeply. The other laughed under his breath while they shook their head.
From the side, Master Shen raised his gourd but didn’t drink. "So," he said lazily, "what’s changed?"
The first to speak was a stocky, bronze-skinned Primarch whose voice carried the resonance of shattered mountains.

"I received theBasic Living Origin Garden Archetype: Warrior.The Garden’s weaving says it’s melee-focused, purely. Resistance Archetype Points will turn it into a juggernaut. Brute force. Massive defense. Close-range superiority. No Weavings of Existence would get past ny defenses once the Garden is cultivated enough."

Next came the lean, emerald-eyed man with sharp features. "Mine’s Basic as well," He said. "Living Origin Garden Archetype: Archer.It’s built for range. With enough Archetype Points, I can shoot through anything. Even the millions of Existential Dimensional Lattices of an Originus Venerant can potentially be pierced through!"
WAA!
Then, the Primarch that Noah had been watching all along stepped forward.
The cube she’d chosen, bearing the frost-rune, had visibly altered her aura.
"I was given something different," she said, breath still uneven. "It’s not Basic. It’s aRare Living Origin Garden Archetype..."
Her voice lowered, like she couldn’t believe her luck.
"Frost Mage."
Around her, cold began to swirl.
Master Shen’s eyes gleamed with interest. "Distribute your points," he said simply. "Let’s see what these Gardens can do when our authorities are nullified."
The Frost Mage Primarch nodded, and then something... shifted as she looked within.
"I feel it," she said, eyes closing. "Inside me... there’s now a garden. A small one. Illusory vines flowing in every direction waiting to be activated."
She paused.
"There are pathways. Points I can place down one after another. Every ten... seems to unlock something significant."
She lifted a hand, and cold gathered.
"Ten points unlocked the first ability. The initial nine increased my levels of Energy and Authority of Living Origin Authority, and the tenth point...a weapon from my Garden. The [Ice Staff Bud]."

A white-blue staff materialized in her hand, its shaft covered in swirling runes that screamed of freezing intent. The runes resembled complex Existential Dimensional Lattices, but none Noah had seen before.
Noah watched closely.
Not common Authority.
Something else entirely.
Living Origin Authority- complex and pure in its own right!
The Primarch continued, her voice hushed with wonder.
"I spent twenty more points. I opened new energy pathways. My Garden responded further. I gained boosts toregeneration, faster existential casting, and speed of attack.Then..."
She raised her hands.
WAA!
Nine spheres of crystallized frost flared into existence and began to orbit her like loyal stars.
"...I unlocked theExclusive Frost Mage Garden Bud: Autonomous Frost Orbs."
The air around her dropped in temperature as her body shimmered with condensed cold, woven by her Living Origin Garden.
The others watched in silence.
Master Shen scratched his chin thoughtfully. "Interesting..."

The Warrior Primarch grunted, slamming a foot into the ground. Crimson runes flared across his arms, and a massive crimson-gold mace formed in his hand. His frame bulged as power coursed through him, his aura like that of a rampaging ancient beast.
Beside him, the Archer Primarch manifested a gleaming verdant bow, humming with verdant threads of light that seemed to lock on to distant targets not even present.

Both of them had unlocked basic Archetypes. Each had between 30 to 60 Resistance Archetype Points, giving them formidable starts, but far from the tier Noah suspected the Masters of Existence would reach.
Still... the power was real.
At such a time.
A cold voice rang out from the side, composed but brimming with subdued authority.
"Go," Master Hannibal commanded. "Test your might. Engage the golems ahead with this new Living Origin Authority. Let us see how the Gardens of those with your level of power perform under pressure."
A beat passed.
The three Primarchs, now brimming with Living Origin Authority and Archetype resonance, shared a look.
Then they stepped forward, moving past the central ring of cubes, crossing into the zone where fifty white-masked crimson gold golems stood tall and silent.
Their crimson-gold armor glinted like molten brass, and none had moved since the beginning.
But now?
Now they stirred.
Noah exhaled softly, his hand tightening slightly on the rope still connected to Sigrid.
This... was about to get interesting.
The three Primarchs stepped beyond the ring of cubes, their new Archetypes pulsing through their bodies like second heartbeats.
The moment their feet crossed the midpoint...
CLANG!
Soundless before, the golems responded.
Fifty crimson-gold titans of seamless armor and porcelain-white masks lit up with eerie sigils, Eyes etched into their chests flaring with Living Origin Authority.
Five of them moved.
Two surged forward with gleaming spears that pulsed with jagged, looping runes.
One slammed down a step, both arms rising as twin tower shields clicked into place with a seismic echo.
Another walked forward with slow, bone-steady weight, hands gripping a massive crossbow that shimmered like it had been forged in the collapse of a dying star.
And the last- a slender, almost serpentine golem, held no weapon. It simply moved, a blur among the stillness, as if made from compressed wind and silence. An assassin.
The Warrior Primarch let out a booming cry as his mace swung forward to meet the twin-shield golem head-on.
"Come, then!"

He crashed into it with titanic force, his crimson runes flaring, but the golem didn’t budge. Its shields held like the side of a mountain as a pulse of Living Origin Authority blasted the Primarch backward, his armor shearing open at the chest.

To the left, the Archer Primarch loosed arrow after arrow, green verdant light streaking forward, only to be shredded mid-air by the spear-wielding golems’ counter-slashes, their weapons humming with runes of disruption.
The Frost Mage surged her frost orbs outward, the nine swirling with blizzards of freezing air that layered around the approaching golems- slowing them, coating them in sheets of glacial breath.
For a moment, it looked like they’d created distance.
For a moment, it seemed like the Gardens might work.
HUUM!
Then...
The crossbow fired.
A single, blazing bolt of condensed crimson gold laced with layered Lattices of Living Origin Authority shattered the still air and...BOOM!
It tore through the Archer Primarch’s shoulder, severing it cleanly and sending her spinning backward with a cry of pain.
Before anyone could react...
Another bolt flew.
This time, it struck the Warrior Primarch in the chest with a terrifying penetrative light amd went straight through.
The defense of his Garden Archetype were not enough!
His expression didn’t even register pain. Just surprise.
Then... nothing.
His body spasmed once before collapsing into the ground.
The Frost Mage turned to retreat, her staff spinning in hand, her frost orbs forming a shield behind her.
But...
Too slow.
The spear-wielding golem vanished from sight and appeared again mid-air.
WOOSH!
The spear whistled through the labyrinth air and landed squarely in her chest, pinning her to the ground like a kebab with a flash of Living Origin Authority so brutal it shattered her Garden!
The ice-blue runes dimmed.
The frost orbs winked out.
She tried to raise her hand one last time...
And then her body fell still.
Silence.
Not a single being moved.
The remaining two golems pulled back.
Their spears and crossbow returning to their neutral positions as they joined the ranks of the still 45, standing like statues, as if nothing had happened.
Three bodies lay in ruin.
Or... they should have.
But before their remains could even settle...
The crimson-gold floor absorbed them.
Where each had fallen, delicate, glowing flowers bloomed in silence- fractal petals of frost, stone, and green life.
Their Gardens.
The only remnants.
Their names, their identities, swallowed by the Labyrinth in mere moments.
Even the air felt changed.
Like something ancient had blinked once and then turned its gaze away again.
Noah didn’t move.

His eyes shone with dangerous calm as he took everything in, the expressions of Primarchs now pale with cold sweat, the stilled posture of Masters of Existence who had finally registered the Labyrinth’s lethality.
Sigrid slowly placed her hand to her mouth, her eyes wide.
She didn’t speak.
Didn’t sign.
Just stared at the flowers, then at the ground, then at the five golems that had casually returned to stillness.
Master Shen lowered his gourd, for once... not smiling.
Master Hannibal’s golden gaze didn’t waver, but his jaw was clenched tight.
Noah, for his part, remained unmoved.
But inside?
Calculations bloomed.
Those golems fought with terrifying power.
Living Origin Authority.
Something with its own Complexity and Purity.
Something deeper!

chapters.title: Chapter 3801: Unique Origin I
paragraphs: Many eyes were still locked on the Gardens.
On what was left of three lives that had just bloomed and vanished in under a minute.
And then, Master Hannibal’s cold voice cut through the reverent silence like the final stroke of a guillotine.
"They have returned to the light of the sun."
He turned, his figure wreathed in a restrained halo of authority.
"Their sacrifices will not be in vain. Now we understand the level of threat before us. Choose your Archetypes."
Without waiting, his body pulsed- dense with power, his golden Lattices like living blades folded over him. His steps did not pause. He moved directly toward the Cubes.
And with that, the spell was broken.
The other Primarchs stirred, the dread in their hearts overtaken by urgency.
The faster they claimed a Cube, the rarer the Archetype, the greater their chance of survival.
Feet began to move.
Rushing. Choosing.
But not Noah.

He walked forward slowly, calmly, his crimson-gold eyes flickering across the field of cubes. A thousand runes within each triangular marking danced before his gaze, ever-changing and difficult even for his mind to fully decipher.
His expression remained unreadable.
Beside him, Sigrid raised her hand to sign something- her face inquisitive.
But before she could begin, Noah glanced over and smiled.
"We’re in a new space now where you have even been able to walk by yourself," he said softly. "Why don’t you try speaking again?"
She blinked.
Then tilted her head.
"...What do you mean...!"
A sound.
A glorious sound!
The sound that came out was music.
Her voice- gentle, melodic, yet piercing with clarity- rippled across the Labyrinth. The very frequency of it tugged at the strings of reality.
Noah’s ears buzzed.
All around, Primarchs stopped mid-step. Heads turned. Eyes widened.
It was as though a celestial choir had spoken into the bones of existence.
Sigrid froze, hands covering her mouth as if she’d said something wrong, then suddenly smiled. Brightly. Radiantly.
"I can hear my voice..."
It was simple.
It was profound.
It was freedom.
"I! Can! Speak!"
Her voice exploded out again, echoing like a siren through the square space.
BZZZT!
The 50 Golems twitched.
They did not act, but many heads turned toward her, those white masks subtly tilting in response.
The room turned tense.
Sigrid shrank slightly as she let out a cough, moving behind Noah protectively.
She scooted closer to Noah again, whispering like someone hiding from trouble.
She whispered to herself to make sure that she really could hear her voice, even musing that this was her voice, even though she did not remember it.
After she confirmed this again and again, she proceeded to look at Noah and ask the question that she had wanted to sign.
"So, um... how many Archetype Points do you have? Mine seem...off."
Noah’s eyes narrowed, tone calm as he replied, "That’s not something we should share out loud."
He looked left and right- Master Shen too engrossed in evaluating Cubes, Master Hannibal radiating sharp intent in his own selection, and then leaned in towards Sigrid.
His hand gently pushed Sigrid’s dark hair back from her ear, his breath brushing lightly against her skin as he whispered.
"I have 200."
A pause.
Her skin felt a tingle as her eyes shone with light.
She then seemingly steeled herself before she looked around with clear eyes to make sure others weren’t listening, and then...
She rose onto her toes as her lips neared his ears, breath warm against his neck as she whispered back...
"If you have 200... then why the heck do I have 500?"
HUUM!
Noah stopped.
His smile didn’t fade.
But his mind sharpened like a tyrannical blade.
Five hundred?
He didn’t react outwardly. He simply walked forward again, steps easy, voice calm.
"...Did you see a message explaining why?"
Sigrid nodded, her brows scrunching in thought. "Yeah. Something like... ’Due to the nature of my Existence, that many Resistance Archetype Points had been obtained..."
She spoke towards him freely as if she fully trusted him.
He said nothing.
But inside?
He recalculated everything.
Her Existence continued to exceed any known norms!
It was unfathomable.
Originus Venerant-tier Points from someone who only recently discovered her own voice?
He whispered without looking at her, "Keep that between us."
"Okay," she whispered back, eyes bright with quiet fire.
Then...
DING!
A prompt surged in front of Noah’s eyes.

|The True Source of Runes, with the support of the True Sources of Origin, Quintessence, Infinity, Paradox, the Protagonist, and more...has analyzed the Living Origin Cubes before you and has identified a singular recommendation.|
Noah’s gaze sharpened.
The True Source of Runes.
His mind sharpened further as he began theorizing about something else he had already began to analyze.
The True Source of Origin.
In this labyrinth, there was only Living Origin Authority that worked through the Living Origin Garden Archetypes.
So...what if his True Source of Origin was...a Living Source?
Would the Living True Source of Origin grant the same power as the Living Origin Authority?
It was a thought.
A glorious thought and possibility as there was no harm putting it to the test!
His Lattices pulsed faintly as he focused across the field of Cubes, past dozens still shimmering, being chosen or hovered over...until his vision locked onto one.
A distant crimson-gold cube.
Sitting quietly. Its triangular rune unmoving.
Unlike the others, which flickered and shifted endlessly, this one had settled.
The triangle at its core burned bright, its edges laced with seven core runes.
And deep within the triangle... a symbol he’d never seen before.
A mark that felt familiar, but defied naming.
As if it didn’t belong in any grandeur of existence.
Noah’s breath left him slowly.
He looked at Sigrid, who tilted her head with a smile as she looked where he was looking. "Are you gonna pick that one?"
Noah smiled back.
Then nodded.
And walked.
Towards the quiet choice.
Toward a Cube that pulsed not with Raw Power or flashy authority.
But with True Power, forged from something even he didn’t fully understand.
Not yet.
Tied to him, Sigrid also looked around as if her eyes told her exactly what cube to choose if Noah chose that other one!

In a short period of time, Noah came in front of a cube that he decisively reached out to, and at the same time...the figure of Sigrid has her eyes light up as she jumped up lightly to touch...another cube nearby as if it was exactly what she wanted!

chapters.title: Chapter 3802: Unique Origin II
paragraphs: A faint chime echoed through the chamber as the choice was made.
He chose it because he trusted his True Sources, and he watched as this entire cube disappeared into his chest and began unfurling into...a Garden.
Glorious in nature.
Vibrant in stature.
He already knew it would not be something Basic.
After all, he was the holder of the Living True Source of Quintessence and Protagonist, how could anything he held be basic?!
HUUM!
|You have obtained the Unique Living Origin Garden Archetype – Runic Battle Mage.|
Noah’s breath pulsed- not in shock, but in quiet satisfaction.
Then it began.

A soft warmth unfolded in his chest, blooming outward like a flower of light. A single bud, crimson-gold and humming with layered power, took root at the very center of his Existence, right above his Living Wheel.
It wasn’t just metaphorical.
He could see it.
Inside his existence, where his True Sources coiled and spun, a new structure now wove between the gaps- foreign, yet familiar. A Runic Garden of Origin.
One with a Unique Archetype!
At its core was the central bud, brilliant and pulsing like the first spark of Origin.

From it, hundreds of illusory vines reached outward, each shimmering with ghostly light. At regular intervals along these vines were plus-shaped runic points, nodes of potential, waiting. A silent invitation to mold the unknown with Points.
It resembled a vast skill tree written in the script of existence itself.
A prompt appeared again.
|A Unique Runic Garden of Origin has bloomed within your Being and is awaiting Resistance Archetype Point distribution.|
Noah took in a long, measured breath, feeling the threads of crimson-gold Lattices brushing against his mind like eager suggestions.
There were many possible areas to add points to.
But before he could act, before he could explore this unfathomable new construct, he felt the pull on the tether at his wrist.
He turned.
Sigrid was standing unnaturally still.
Her gaze wasn’t focused on the surroundings or even her own chest that was now shining. It was far-off, distant.
Her fingers twitched. Her lips parted.
Noah narrowed his eyes. "What is it?"
She blinked.
And then, something shifted.

"I... remembered something," she said slowly. Her voice was quieter now, distant but focused. "Something... about Origin. But it doesn’t make sense. It was like a story. A story I never heard before but somehow... I know it."
A cold light traveled down Noah’s eyes as he asked, "What story?"
Sigrid turned to him, eyes now sharp with a clarity that hadn’t been there a second ago.
And she began to speak as if she were possessed.
"In the Earliest Folds of Existence, before Threads had form and Time had purpose, there was a Creature.
It had no name.
It had no path.
It simply... wandered.
Through the fog of Unwritten Existences, it moved with patient steps and a quiet curiosity.
But it was aimless and with no purpose as it began to feel a vast sense of emptiness. An emptiness that only grew.
A loneliness as vast as the folds of existence.
One day, the Creature came upon something it had never seen before: a small glowing orb that pulsed with rhythmic, living light.
It was warm.
Comforting.
It radiated purpose.
The Creature gazed at it for a long while, then asked gently.
’What are you?’
And the orb answered.
"I am the memory of structure. The will to begin. I am the Living Origin."
The Creature tilted its head, watching the light, its mind already churning. ’And what does one do... with a beginning?’
"You cultivate it," the Origin replied. "You plant it within yourself and allow it to grow. You become more."
The Creature sat.
Listened.
Its gaze was unblinking, not with reverence, but with thought.
And then, as if sensing the potential weight of a decision, a second presence began to manifest.
Another orb.
It did not arrive, it unwrote the space it entered as if it were inevitable.
It was another orb.
It was cold.
Endless.
Uncertain.
It was...the Living Paradox.
The Creature watched it form, its body was shifting contradiction, its edges too sharp, its core too deep.
The Living Paradox said nothing at first.
Then, it spoke in tones that seemed to come from everywhere and nowhere.
’Why do you seek a beginning?’
The Creature took its time, then answered softly. ’Because even unshaped clay may wish to know the shape it could hold.’

The Paradox sneered. ’The Living Origin will offer you roots, but also limits. If you take me instead, you will become something without limits. Something that contradicts being. Something that defies sense.’
The Living Origin pulsed, silent and steady.
The Creature stood, calm in the face of both extremes.
It looked at the Living Paradox and said, ’There is power in the undefined. But not all that is undefined must be embraced. I seek to understand. And to understand, I must first begin.’
The Paradox’s form was unbearably cold as in the next moment, it unraveled and vanished with a sound like a scream swallowed by time.
And in the silence left behind, the Living Origin hovered closer.
The Creature extended its hand.
And for the first time in that ancient, directionless era...
A Garden bloomed. An Origin was grasped.
A single root took hold.
It was a beginning, but it had its limits.
And the Creature, nameless and quiet, survived the Earliest Folds of Existence.
Not because it was powerful.
But because it chose to begin."
HUUUM!
Sigrid’s final words floated into silence.
The tale of the nameless Creature and the Living Origin echoed no longer, and yet... its weight lingered. Heavy. Reverberating like an unstruck gong inside every fold of the chamber.
She blinked slowly, as though waking from a dream. Her eyes cleared, her breath caught.
And only then did she realize.
Everyone was staring at her.
Not just Noah.
Every Primarch in the square.
Even Masters Shen and Hannibal stood silent.
Their eyes... unsettled.
Like they’d just glimpsed behind the veil of Existence and seen something that wasn’t meant to be seen.
Something no entity was supposed to hear.
Not here.
Not now.
Sigrid’s voice faltered into the air, the earlier joy at reclaiming her voice fading under the growing weight of realization.
She slowly stepped back, slipping behind Noah’s figure like a child seeking shelter from an unseen storm.
"Was the story... that scary?" she asked quietly, as if afraid her voice alone might cause another disturbance.
Noah didn’t answer immediately.
His expression was calm, almost gentle.
But his mind was burning.
What the fuck was that?
The Earliest Fold of Existence?
A Creature that chose the Living Origin?
A Living Paradox that... challenged that choice?
Her story hadn’t been innocent.
It hadn’t been metaphor.
It seemed more like a memory.
A story of something that had happened, and was passed down. Not invented, but a true Record!
He could feel it in his Existence.
It wasn’t fiction.
It was history from a time before history.
"...It was fine," Noah said softly, voice as calm as glass. "Just... unexpected."
Sigrid’s shoulders eased slightly, still tucked behind him.
But Noah remained still, his gaze slowly sweeping the room.
The Primarchs had gone rigid.
Their gardens still shimmered, still pulsing faintly with Living Origin energy, but none were cultivating.
None were distributing their Resistance Archetype Points.
They had all frozen after the tale.
Even Master Hannibal had stopped. The cube he’d chosen was fusing to his chest, but the light in his eyes was unfathomably bright. His gaze? Cold. Calculating. But unreadable.
And Master Shen...
He had tilted his head slightly, as if listening to music only he could hear.
Noah turned inward again, reaching toward the roots now pulsing within his chest.
The Runic Battle Mage Archetype, its garden still blooming, still waiting.
Still untouched.
And yet, his thoughts weren’t on skill branches or runes.
They were on the story.
The Living Origin. The Living Paradox.
What if these weren’t just types of power?
What if they weren’t just Authority classifications?
What if they were...Entities? And not in the sense of Foldless Ones being Living Paradoxes.
What if they were States of Being? Or the oldest concepts of Existence?
Noah’s eyes slowly narrowed.
He didn’t know the full answer.
Not yet.
But a part of him whispered, calm and absolute, that the path forward now required more than just survival.
It required understanding.
And understanding meant unraveling what the Living Origin really was...before the Living Paradox found them first.
Whether that Living Paradox would be the Foldless Ones, or something even more Unfathomable!
The chamber remained unnervingly silent.
But beneath that silence, in the trembling gardens of every soul here...
The seeds of dread had already taken root.

chapters.title: Chapter 3803: Unique Origin III
paragraphs: The silence hung like a drop of water on a blade until Noah’s voice, steady and dry, finally cut through it.
"The words of a being with no memory are unique, aren’t they?" he said, his tone almost casual. "Lets not pay too much heed to them, hmm?"
He gestured lightly with his hand toward the distance. "We’ve still got nine treasure chests waiting for us. Full of unknown wonders..."
A ripple spread through the square.
A release.
The tension didn’t vanish, but it loosened. Like fingers uncurled from a blade’s hilt.
Eyes shifted back to Gardens.
Hands began to rise toward Cubes again.
But the tale of the Creature, Living Origin, and Living Paradox lingered in their minds.
Even Master Shen exhaled, as though coming back to himself, muttering...that he needed a drink.
Master Hannibal, however, lingered. His eyes stayed locked on Sigrid for a breath too long- sharp and clinical.
And then he turned coldly, moving away.
Noah, sensing it all, nudged Sigrid gently with his elbow.
"Come on. Nurture your Garden," he said with a light smile.
But then he paused, something sharp flickering behind his eyes. "Speaking of which... what’s yours?"
Sigrid hesitated, then leaned closer. Her voice barely above a whisper.
"...It said I got the Exclusive Living Origin Garden Archetype- Mother of Origin."
Noah blinked once.
Then twice.
Exclusive.
His was Unique, already beyond comprehension.
But Exclusive?
It may be something entirely meant for her in this whole place.
His gaze sharpened instinctively, reading her features anew. But she didn’t even understand what that classification meant.
She looked almost apologetic for speaking it aloud.
He forced the tension in his shoulders to relax and smiled.
"Good," he said gently. "Then nurture it. Carefully. Just follow your instincts. "
He turned back toward his own Garden, the weight of the moment returning to his chest as he inhaled and focused inward.
The Living Origin Garden of the Runic Battle Mage bloomed inside him like a glowing crimson-gold sigil embedded over his Living Wheel.
Nine vines sprouted from the central bud, each one arching into space like radiant rivers of potential.
Each vine bore nine glowing nodes that were crimson-gold plus signs lined like beads of fate.
And each vine terminated... in something greater.
An Origin Ability.
He reached toward the first vine.
Its flow pulsed with vibrant energy, and as he brushed his consciousness along the nodes, knowledge flowed.
|+100 Living Origin Energy and +50 Living Origin Vigor|
Simple.
Foundational.
The numbers increased per node. Adding and Multiplying.
But the tenth node... burned brighter.
|[Runic Enhancement: Origin Skin] - Enchants your body with a reactive weave of Runic Origin Lattices of Defense. Gain passive resistance to Origin damage.|
"...Not bad," Noah murmured as he looked at this pathway.
He moved on.
The second vine gave him a slightly different feeling. Faster. Hotter.
|+200 Living Origin Energy and +10 Living Origin Vigor|
The imbalance was obvious. A more volatile path where energy was even more favored.
And the tenth node?

|[Runic Battle Skill: Fireball] - Launch a compressed rune-inscribed flame that scales with Living Origin Energy. With enough advancement of the Living Origin Garden Archetype- Runic Battle Mage, even the output of the Flame of Origin that birthed Wheels of Existence is possible to unleash.|
"Fireball..."
Noah said under his breath.
And paused.
A long, quiet pause.
He smiled, slow and genuine.
Because once, long ago, in a ruined apartment of his old world, that had been his first skill.
When mana had first coursed through him.
When his fingers had trembled with the weight of power for the first time, and all he could do was hurl flames at his enemies endlessly.
Fireball.
The path was different now, more profound, but that root?
That Origin?
It was always fire.
He touched the first plus sign on this vine.
Just one point for now so that he knew exactly where to continue.
He then gazed at the other pathways.
The third vine pulsed with a different hue altogether.
Heavy. Rooted.
|+10 Living Origin Energy and +200 Living Origin Vigor|
The tenth node on this vine displayed...

|[Runic Ward: Anchor Glyph] - Generate a Living Origin rune that roots in a chosen location. Reduces damage taken by you and your allies within range and anchors spells cast in the area, increasing their effectiveness. Gain 10% Regeneration of Energy and Vigor every minute.|
He nodded in appreciation.
And he looked at the other possible pathways.
Each vine was a philosophy. A doctrine.
And every step along them changed the foundation of his being inside this Labyrinth.
The possibilities... were immense.
But for now?
He looked back again at that second vine.
The one with the Fireball.
He added a second point.
Then a third.
Then a fourth.
Each one pulsed into his Garden, the vine glowing more brightly with every step.
The garden beginning to bloom ever so slowly!
The Runic Battle Mage of the Living Origin had begun to awaken!
Sixth Point!
Ninth Point!
Tenth Point!
The tenth pulse settled into place.
Noah’s breath flowed out like quiet steam as the final node along the second vine bloomed with light inside his Garden.
He felt it before he saw it.
A distinct change in the texture of reality around his body, like the thrum of potential coiling tighter.
Then...
HUUM!
A crimson-gold rune ignited on the back of his right hand, curling into a complex sigil that pulsed with Living Origin Authority.
The air shimmered faintly.
The rune wasn’t passive. Every breath he took fueled it. Every thought shaped it.
This wasn’t just an ability.
It was his Origin taking form.
He turned his mind inward.
The Garden of the Runic Battle Mage hummed with completion- ten points along the second vine activated, unlocking his first Battle Skill.
And with that, a Runic Status Panel shimmered into being before his eyes, something he compiled based on the 10 Resistance Archetype Points he had used so far, with 190 remaining!
Name: Noah Osmont
Living Origin Garden Archetype: Unique – Runic Battle Mage
Living Origin Energy: 1800
Living Origin Vigor: 90
Archetype Resistance Points Used: 10 (Vine II – Offensive Origin Path)
Runic Battle Skills Unlocked: [Runic Battle Skill: Fireball]
The numbers matched perfectly. Numbers of a glass cannon.

Each of the nine foundational nodes along the second vine had granted him +200 Living Origin Energy and +10 Vigor. Cumulatively, they now surged in his core, shaping his power applicable here from the inside out!

chapters.title: Chapter 3804: Unique Origin IV
paragraphs: The moment Noah invested the tenth point and awakened Fireball, the vine he had been feeding responded with renewed vigor.
The Garden became bigger.
The Living Origin Authority within him increased!
The length of the vine stretched, the runes along it multiplying. Three new paths lit up beyond the Fireball node, each radiating a distinct hue and essence.
He scanned them swiftly.
One pulsed with kinetic rhythm, a streak of motion encoded into light. Its nodes shimmered with inscriptions of +3% Increased Origin Cast Speed and Origin Attack Speed.
The second glowed deep with Living Origin Energy, its nodes cycling in steady pulses- +200 Energy per point.
The third carried weight, +200 Living Origin Vigor, its glyphs dark and grounding like the runes carved into mountain roots.
He didn’t hesitate.
Speed was control.
And control was everything.
His mind reached for the first kinetic node, and it welcomed him.
+3% Origin Cast Speed and Origin Attack Speed.
Then the next.
And the next.

The pulses cascaded, each node breathing more rhythm into his form. His weavings of Existence sharpened. His vessels, arteries, and stellar capillaries forged by a Heart of Infinity and a Living Wheel of Existence now coursed with Living Origin Authority freely as if they were being built for it, making its coursing unimaginably faster!
He continued adding Points to these nodes until the 29th was lit up brightly.
And then...
The thirtieth node glowed.
It was different.
It did not bear numbers.
It bore a name.

[Runic Origin Flame Aura]:: You exude an active aura formed of Living Origin Flame, inscribed with layered Runic Weavings. While passive enemies within 25 meters suffer -45% resistance to Origin Damage and are periodically ignited with flame runes that detonate after 2 seconds, dealing fire damage based on your Living Origin Energy. This Aura also empowers your Runic Battle Skills, granting them +45% area of effect and 45% increased detonation speed. Only three Runic Auras may be active at a time.
WAA!
The moment he unlocked it, a radiant sigil appeared over his chest, it’s outer circle a blazing ouroboros of fire runes, rotating slowly beneath his skin like a sun drawn from runic scripture.
The aura hadn’t even been fully activated yet, but its presence was enough to make the very space around him waver as a burst of crimson gold heat burst from him!
The vine pulsed once more, and now, two new branching paths split from the awakened Runic Origin Flame Aura node.

One began with an increase of Living Origin Energy, Vigor, and combinations of Cast Speed and Attack Speed as he made the choices based on intuition, continuing to select nodes until he reached...the 60th Node, which granted a Runic Battle Skill- [Origin Rune Brand]
HUUM!
The entire vine flared with resonance, and another Rune engraved itself into the mental fabric of his inner Garden!

[Runic Battle Skill: Origin Rune Brand]:: You passively generate branded Origin Runes. Whenever any form of enemy energy- physical, metaphysical, mental, spiritual, or dimensional- comes into contact with your Being, the source is branded with a single Origin Rune. A branded target has the rune explode after a nanosecond delay, dealing 200% Living Origin Damage in a cascading detonation that disrupts spellcasting and mobility. This effect scales with your Cast Speed and can occur multiple times per second.
The glowing rune appeared above Noah’s collarbone, etched into the space between his throat and shoulder like a sigil stitched in light.
It pulsed once.
Then vanished beneath his skin.
But he felt it.
The moment energy touched him- even from observation, even from intent- something would be branded, and a fiery hell would bloom.
A silent warning wrapped in beauty.
He continued, pushing deeper down the vine!
The following nodes flowed in rhythm- alternating bonuses in Living Origin Energy, Living Origin Vigor, and Increased Origin Cast and Attack Speed.
His core bloomed brighter.
His weavings gradually felt invincible as they were getting filled with Living Origin Authority!
Because he had now spent nearly 90 points which would be equivalent to a Primarch with 90% Resistance!
Until...
The 100th node on this advanced path revealed itself.
But instead of an ability or a passive stat, it bore a singular, pulsing phrase etched in deep-blue crystalline runes unlike any he’d seen before.
[Living Origin Resistance]:: You carry a spark that resists even the Source itself. Grants +25% Origin Resistance. The path you walk now resists even the foundations of what birthed it.
Noah froze.
The Garden trembled faintly as his awareness spun inward, and immediately, a notification shimmered into existence, this time from outside the Garden interface.
His original Existential Status Panel reappeared.
And beneath the category of True Absolute Existential Resistances, he saw it.
Where it had read- Origin Resistance: 10%
Now...
Origin Resistance: 35%
An unfathomable gain.
A ridiculous capability!
This wasn’t a bonus from a loot cache.
This was a direct upgrade to his core Authority- one of his ten Resistances!
And now?
His Origin Resistance...had tripled!
He looked around him.
The Living Origin Labyrinth... held secrets even he hadn’t calculated.
And if this was only the 100th node?
Then what lay deeper?
The Garden inside pulsed once more as it had grown tremendously now.

His existence felt the foreign yet familiar Living Origin Authority coursing through him as he felt like if he went against the Living Origin Golems in the distance, he may not need to be fearful of them!
But it did not seem like he was the only one with this idea.

He looked up as he saw Master Hannibal...already moving ahead at the forefront, his body pulsing with terrifying waves of Living Origin Authority as 3 golden hammers and 3 golden shields surrounded him!
Master Hannibal was already moving.
Not running.
Not walking.
Just advancing.
Like a gravitational inevitability.
Three radiant hammers of golden fire spun around his frame, each one inscribed with triangular runes that sang with judgment.
Opposite them, three golden shields rotated, forming a perfect celestial defense, orbiting his body with seamless, geometric discipline.
He did not speak.
He did not gesture.
He simply entered the arena of death past where the Cubes were.
He crossed the line alone.
And the Labyrinth responded!
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 3805: Fire I
paragraphs: The Golems came to life.
The same five Living Origin Golems that had eviscerated the three Primarchs emerged from the crimson-gold stillness.
The dual-spear bearers.
The twin-shield juggernaut.
The silent assassin.
The radiant crossbow sniper.
Their masks glowed white-hot.
Their Authority surged.
But Master Hannibal?
He did not flinch!
He was an Originus Venerant entity.
And he had a glorious purpose. Even those behind him did not know the weight he bore!
The first spear-wielding golem surged toward him.
It never reached.
BOOM!

A hammer blurred out like a thunderbolt, colliding with the golem’s chest and detonating Living Origin Authority in a geyser of molten force. The white mask cracked, splintered, and exploded outward in shards as the golem folded inward with a wet crunch.
The second spear wielder swept in low, but it was too late.
A shield spiraled down with surgical speed, flattening the golem’s skull into the floor with a sickening snap.
The juggernaut lifted its twin shields and launched forward.
Master Hannibal met it head-on.
He didn’t sidestep.
He stepped in.
One hammer flared with blazing white-gold. He slammed it into the center of the golem’s shields.
CRACK!
Both shields shattered.
The force sent stone, bone-like alloy, and molten Origin weavings flying across the field.
Hannibal followed with a rotating elbow to the golem’s chin, then jammed a second hammer straight through its throat, blowing it apart.
The crossbow golem fired.
Three shots.
All deflected- ricocheting off his spinning shields in a flash of precision so cold it felt premeditated.
The crossbow itself never got to reload.
A hammer streaked from Hannibal’s side and caved in the golem’s skull, sending its massive metal body flipping end over end like a collapsing cathedral.
Only the assassin remained.
It was fast. Too fast.
It blinked behind him.
But Hannibal spun before it arrived.
A golden shield detached and intercepted the blade mid-air, the collision ringing like cracked glass. With his free hand, Hannibal grabbed the assassin golem by the face...and crushed it.
Fingers clenched. Runes flared.
The mask burst. Then the head. Then the spine of the golem.
One-handed. Effortless.
Bloodlike energy sprayed from ruptured Origin cores as all five golems fell in under six seconds.
But he wasn’t done.
Not even close.
From deeper within the chamber they were in...
Ten more Golems surged forward, their armor humming with Living Origin Authority.
Some glided.
Some bounded.
One slithered like a fusion of serpent and machine, its body formed of coiled runic wire and spike-covered muscle.
Hannibal inhaled once.
The hammers stopped orbiting.
A Runic Battle Skill was likely activated.
And...
CRACK—!
BOOM—!
A massive golden hammer bloomed in the space above and crashed down over everything, releasing holy goldeb waves of light that spread out like a sea formed of smaller hammers and shield.
In every direction, golden arcs of Living Origin burst outward. Every hammer was a headshot. Every shield was a parry. Every step Hannibal took left a dead Golem in its wake.
One tried to form a barrier of twisting vines- he spun through it, hammer-first, smashing through both the spell and the caster’s chest in one strike.
Another fired condensed beams of Origin Light.
He reflected the first with a shield, absorbed the second with a spinning guard rune, then speared his shield through the caster’s throat, pinning it into the ground like a ritual.
More came.
Five. Ten. Fifteen.
The full tide.
The entire arena surged with all remaining 50 Living Origin Golems, bursting out in droves- some armored like titans, others with claws like manticores, some casting illusions or ripples of flames.
And Hannibal?
He still didn’t pause.
He slid under one, severed its limbs.
Jumped off another, caving its back.
Dismantled the fourth with one rotating series of shield bashes that shattered its faceplate, then drove his knee upward into the exposed core, ripping it free with his bare hand.
Blood and shards of authority rained in every direction.
The ground, once pristine, was now painted in molten gore and fractured runes.
His hammers moved like celestial executioners, bursting skulls with thunder and tyranny.
His shields spun like sawblades, shattering ribs and warping heads.
Every motion was clean. Calculated. Cruel.
One golem tried to bellow out before he bisected it vertically with a hammer strike that left its body twitching in two.
And finally...
Silence.
Heavy, immense, silence.
The last Golem fell with a metallic gasp, its core caving inward before shattering into flaming particles.
Blood pooled at Master Hannibal’s feet.
Fifty bodies lay scattered around him- gutted, pulverized, silenced.
And still...
His face didn’t change.
Not even a twitch.
Only his golden eyes narrowed slightly as he looked ahead, across the steaming graveyard he had carved, to the nine treasure chests at the end of the arena.
Each one pulsing with sealed power.
Each one waiting.
At this time...
HUUM!
Above Master Hannibal, golden words appeared.
[+5 Resistance Archetype Points]
Words that caused Master Shen and others to stare in shock and eagerness!
Master Hannibal did not change his gaze.
He took a single step forward.
The air burned around him.
And every being still watching...
Held their breath.
In the distance, Noah watched and analyzed everything with cold calculation.
Thereafter, he walked forward in silence.
The air was still thick with residual fire and ruin from Hannibal’s massacre, the floor littered with mangled golem remains that shimmered faintly with dissipating runes of Living Origin.
His eyes, calm and cold, scanned the aftermath.
Hannibal had to have used 200 to 300 points. At least.
That was the only reasonable assumption.
The coordination between the six golden constructs, the fluidity of his casting, and the brutal efficiency of every kill- those weren’t the product of a basic Archetype either.
That was a refined, near-perfect distribution along multiple vines, perhaps more than one fully unlocked Branch.
His Garden was likely monstrous.
Even the Golems adjusted their tactics halfway through... and still died.
Behind him, a few murmurs stirred the silence.
Master Shen let out a low whistle as he moved, the Primarchs following alongside him.
They walked cautiously through the wreckage, eyes flicking toward Hannibal’s back as he stood unmoving before the nine gleaming treasure chests.
Noah moved alongside them all.
His gaze was sharper now.
There were truths hidden in this Labyrinth- real ones.
And some of those truths... walked beside him.
Because to his right, Sigrid glided forward like a flicker of living scripture- swirling with unique waves of crimson-gold Living Origin Authority that pulsed in uneven rhythms.
Her steps were light.
But her eyes?
Distant.
Noah frowned.
He reached out with a measured hand and gently touched her shoulder.
She jolted softly, blinking up at him as if waking from a dream.
"Did you remember something else about you?" he asked quietly.
She stared at him.
Then shook her head.
"No," she whispered. "It’s not about me. It’s about that story again. About...Origin. And the Creature. They seem to come the more I come in contact with this Living Origin Authority."
Noah’s gaze sharpened instantly.

The first story she told had already left ripples in the hearts of Primarchs. It had frozen even Master Hannibal. A memory of the Earliest Folds of Existence, spoken like truth rather than something fake.
And now...
There was more?
He spoke low, threading his voice beneath the attention of others as it rang directly in her ears.
"Tell me. Just me."
She nodded.
Then, softly- impossibly softly- her voice reached only his ears.
It wasn’t sound.
It was Living Origin Authority woven into speech, traveling through the tether of resonance between them.
As if it was only natural for her to do this.
And as they walked across the fractured chamber, her words returned to that strange time before Time.
"After the Creature chose the Living Origin...it continued to walk.
Its form pulsed faintly now- no longer aimless, but full of quiet fire.
It had obtained a beginning.
And with it, purpose.
A desire, faint but burning- To understand. To become more.
But though it felt this purpose...
It could not act upon it.
Every time it reached outward, its limbs failed.
Every time it imagined doing, it faltered.
No tools.
No motion.
Only a growing ache of stillness.
It had a reason to move, but not the means.
And so, the Creature wandered, purpose and Origin clutched tightly to its chest like a dying ember.
One day, in the ever-shifting haze of the Earliest Folds of Existence, it stepped into a realm of madness.
A place without light or structure.
A place where Mutated Inevitabilities roamed.
They were not beings.
They were...hungers made flesh. Things born of failed threads and collapsed purposes. They did not think. They did not reason.
They only devoured.
And the moment they sensed the pulse of Living Origin within the Creature, they surged.
The Creature ran.
It ran endlessly.
Across seas of unborn folds, across mountains of screaming entropy.
It fled for years, never stopping, its beginning burning ever brighter- beacon and curse as millions of Mutated Inevitabilities followed it now.
But it could do nothing but run.
It had purpose, but no claws.
It had beginning, but no force.
And it began to hate.
It hated its stillness.
It hated its helplessness.
And in that moment of despair...
A ripple.
A laugh.
The Living Paradox appeared.
Like oil sliding across untouched canvas.
Its body was chaos made beautiful, contradiction incarnate.
It floated beside the Creature and sneered.
"Do you see now?" it whispered. "You have purpose. You have Origin. But still, you have nothing to act with."
The Creature stared ahead, breathing heavy, but it said nothing.

"I can save you," said the Paradox. "But you must give up your beginning. Let go of the weight of structure. Let go of this foolish thing you cling to. Embrace contradiction... and I will give you power."
The Creature trembled.
It had just obtained its purpose and beginning. It did not want to give it up.
So it did not answer.
Not then.
Not yet.
Instead, it continued running.
Until after an unknown amount of time, it found folds of endless blue.
Ahead, a radiant cerulean sea shimmered in the folds- impossibly still.
It leapt into it, sinking deep.
And within its depths...
It found a third orb.
Smaller than the others. Smaller than Origin and Paradox that had even following the Creature here with a sneer.
The third orb was glowing with endless fractals of color, as if each thought it inspired could birth wonders.
The orb spoke.
"I am the Living Concept."
"...Another?" the Creature whispered, weary and tired.
"I am the shape of imagination. The whisper that defines action. I am... potential."
The orb circled the Creature slowly.
"I can join you and the Origin. And with me, I will give you the means to act. But I will need... something."
"...What?"
"Your imagination. The power of interpretation."
The Creature recoiled.
Another cost?
Why?
Why did everything beyond the Living Origin demand something?
"What is this Existence," the Creature asked, "where every step forward requires pain? Where everything has a price?"
And from the shadows...
The Living Paradox laughed again.
It hovered behind them both, smiling wide.
And in a voice as old as contradiction, it said:
"Because that is the first truth of existence."
"Everything comes at a cost."
The Creature turned back to the Living Concept.
"...Then tell me," it said softly. "What is it... about you... that gives me the power to act?"
The Living Concept pulsed, radiant and steady.
And in a voice that was both whisper and law, it answered.
"Inside of me... dwells Mana."
"The engine of all action."
HUUM!
The cerulean sea was still.
And in its depths, the Living Concept hovered silently, pulsing with infinite potential- like a nebula folded into a single thought.
The Creature said nothing for a long time.
It simply floated.
Thinking.
Burning.
Weeping, though it had no eyes to weep with.
This was its second chance.
Another choice.
The Living Origin had given it purpose.
But purpose without power was cruelty.
And now?
Now there was a path.
But it came with a cost.
Imagination, or his purpose.
A part of the Creature stirred in defiance.
But a deeper part... one carved by years of running, of helplessness, of screaming silently against inevitability...
That part stepped forward.
And whispered, "Take it. Take my imagination."
The Living Concept pulsed with solemn light.
And then it moved.
It pressed gently into the core of the Creature’s Existence, intertwining with the light of the Living Origin still pulsing there.
No fusion.
No explosion.
Just...
Integration.
As if it had always been meant.
A second root joined the first.
Living Origin.
And now, Living Concept.
Two orbs.
Two truths.
Two states of being.
And the cost?
The Creature felt it immediately.
Its thoughts became... simpler.
It no longer wondered what a sound might mean or why the folds of light rippled across the air in beautiful shapes.
That inner curiosity, the flickering dreamlight of imagination, dimmed.
But in its place?
Came structure.
Form.
Power.
And above all...
A pulse.
A surge.
A new heartbeat.
Something liquid flowed within the Creature now- hotter than stars, purer than light.
It did not burn.
It moved.
It obeyed.
It was...
Mana.
HUUMMMMM!
The Creature opened its hands.
And acted.
For the first time in its existence, it shaped a flame.
Not imagined.
Not dreamed.
But real.
It pulled from its Living Origin, the memory of structure, and wove it with Living Concept, the meaning behind creation.
And from their union...
Mana surged.
A radiant sphere of blue-white power bloomed in the Creature’s palm, humming with layered rings of definition and intent.
It pulsed once.
Then again.
And the folds of existence bent around it.
The Creature lifted its head.
It could still feel them- the Mutated Inevitabilities, still lurking, still hungering, still chasing.
They had chased it across eternities.
But now?
It would no longer run.
Now it could act.
Now it could fight.
And the flame in its hand...
Was only the beginning."
BOOM!
Sigrid’s voice faded again.
Noah didn’t speak.
Couldn’t.
Her tale echoed within him like a foundational equation- a principle of power etched deeper than memory.
He looked straight ahead, his Runic Garden still burning behind his ribs.
He felt it now.
More than ever.
Mana.
Oh, Mana!
Was what he had...the same Mana as what the Creature had that allowed him to act all those years ago?!

sentences.text: The Golems came to life.
The same five Living Origin Golems that had eviscerated the three Primarchs emerged from the crimson-gold stillness.

The twin-shield juggernaut.
The silent assassin.
The radiant crossbow sniper.
Their masks glowed white-hot.
Their Authority surged.

He was an Originus Venerant entity.

Even those behind him did not know the weight he bore!
The first spear-wielding golem surged toward him.
It never reached.
BOOM!
A hammer blurred out like a thunderbolt, colliding with the golem’s chest and detonating Living Origin Authority in a geyser of molten force.
The white mask cracked, splintered, and exploded outward in shards as the golem folded inward with a wet crunch.
The second spear wielder swept in low, but it was too late.
A shield spiraled down with surgical speed, flattening the golem’s skull into the floor with a sickening snap.
The juggernaut lifted its twin shields and launched forward.
Master Hannibal met it head-on.
He didn’t sidestep.
He stepped in.
One hammer flared with blazing white-gold.
He slammed it into the center of the golem’s shields.
CRACK!
Both shields shattered.
The force sent stone, bone-like alloy, and molten Origin weavings flying across the field.

Three shots.
All deflected- ricocheting off his spinning shields in a flash of precision so cold it felt premeditated.
The crossbow itself never got to reload.
A hammer streaked from Hannibal’s side and caved in the golem’s skull, sending its massive metal body flipping end over end like a collapsing cathedral.
Only the assassin remained.
It was fast.
Too fast.
It blinked behind him.
But Hannibal spun before it arrived.
A golden shield detached and intercepted the blade mid-air, the collision ringing like cracked glass.
With his free hand, Hannibal grabbed the assassin golem by the face...and crushed it.
Fingers clenched.
Runes flared.
The mask burst.
Then the head.
Then the spine of the golem.
One-handed.
Effortless.
Bloodlike energy sprayed from ruptured Origin cores as all five golems fell in under six seconds.
But he wasn’t done.
Not even close.
From deeper within the chamber they were in...
Ten more Golems surged forward, their armor humming with Living Origin Authority.
Some glided.
Some bounded.
One slithered like a fusion of serpent and machine, its body formed of coiled runic wire and spike-covered muscle.
Hannibal inhaled once.
The hammers stopped orbiting.
A Runic Battle Skill was likely activated.

BOOM—!
A massive golden hammer bloomed in the space above and crashed down over everything, releasing holy goldeb waves of light that spread out like a sea formed of smaller hammers and shield.

Every shield was a parry.
Every step Hannibal took left a dead Golem in its wake.

Another fired condensed beams of Origin Light.

More came.
Five.
Ten.
Fifteen.
The full tide.
The entire arena surged with all remaining 50 Living Origin Golems, bursting out in droves- some armored like titans, others with claws like manticores, some casting illusions or ripples of flames.
And Hannibal?
He still didn’t pause.
He slid under one, severed its limbs.
Jumped off another, caving its back.
Dismantled the fourth with one rotating series of shield bashes that shattered its faceplate, then drove his knee upward into the exposed core, ripping it free with his bare hand.
Blood and shards of authority rained in every direction.
The ground, once pristine, was now painted in molten gore and fractured runes.
His hammers moved like celestial executioners, bursting skulls with thunder and tyranny.
His shields spun like sawblades, shattering ribs and warping heads.
Every motion was clean.
Calculated.
Cruel.
One golem tried to bellow out before he bisected it vertically with a hammer strike that left its body twitching in two.

Silence.
Heavy, immense, silence.
The last Golem fell with a metallic gasp, its core caving inward before shattering into flaming particles.
Blood pooled at Master Hannibal’s feet.
Fifty bodies lay scattered around him- gutted, pulverized, silenced.
And still...
His face didn’t change.
Not even a twitch.
Only his golden eyes narrowed slightly as he looked ahead, across the steaming graveyard he had carved, to the nine treasure chests at the end of the arena.
Each one pulsing with sealed power.
Each one waiting.
At this time...
HUUM!
Above Master Hannibal, golden words appeared.

The air burned around him.

Held their breath.
