You ask me what I am and do all this...because an Inevitability didn’t rise between us?"
Moiraine’s expression did not shift, but the stillness became heavier around her as she gazed at him up and down.
Her voice, when it came, was low and without edge.
"When Paradoxes resonate, Inevitabilities arise.
Always.
Without fail."
She paused, as if reviewing a truth etched into the foundations of the Fold itself.
"For one not to appear...means you are not one of us.
You are not a Living Paradox."
The Fold itself dimmed in response to the implication.
And yet Noah looked at them coldly, his own mind buzzing with possibilities as he replied calmly.
"But I am, though?"
Behind her, Oryzarakh’s glow pulsed once.
"I verified him," the Primordial Foldless One intoned, his voice like gravitational collapse shaped into words.
"I observed...no deception.
No distortion.
But..."
And yet, doubt laced his timeless tone!
Moiraine did not glance at him.
She raised one hand- smooth, deliberate, royal.
"If you are what you claim, this will not harm you."
She spoke two words that seemed to pull gravity into them, her body radiating waves of heavy authority that Noah could barely analyze.
"Schrödinger’s Box."
HUUM!
The atmosphere folded.
Reality twisted and resolved as all nearby weavings buzzed and shook.
An obsidian box gradually took form, its edges paradoxical and absolute.
Its surfaces showed nothing and everything, reflecting Wheels of Existence and Null simultaneously.
It closed around Noah as it contained an undeniable complexity and purity he could currently not deny!
It did not slam shut.
It did not lock.
It simply...was.
Schrödinger.
Paradoxical.
Glorious!
Moiraine’s voice echoed within it with a voice of final examination, her voice steady with suspicion but also...expectation.
As if she wanted to be wrong!
"If you are truly paradoxical...then within this box, you are both alive and dead.
You should both hear me and not.
You should answer and remain silent."
A pause.
"Can you answer me?"
Silence.
A heavy, suffocating silence!
The Foldless Ones stood without motion.
Their authority did not flicker.
Their forms did not shift.
And then...
"Of course I can hear you."
BOOM!
Moiraine’s eyes widened with a glorious light at such words, her expression showing a sense of surprise!
With a single motion of her palm, the obsidian box deconstructed.
Its pieces dissipated like principles rewritten into void.
Noah was still chained.
Still unmoving.
Still bleeding.
But his golden gaze remained calm.
Too calm.
As if he was demanding an explanation!
Moiraine looked at him in silence as if she was still assessing what all of this could mean.
Oryzarakh, looming, was also silent.
And at times, silence alone was able to say a great deal of things.
Moiraine turned to him with gravity in every syllable.
"Seal these region of the Folds.
Reinforce the structure across all weavings of Existence and make sure nothing leaks out.
And begin setting up a Transcendence Foldpath immediately."
No hesitation.
No drama.
Just execution.
Oryzarakh gave no reply.
He vanished right away, folding through unseen geometry and complexity.
And around Noah, the paradox-forged chains began to fall apart, unraveling in strands of luminescent light as he was freed!
The prison platform dimmed once more into silence.
Noah floated still and composed as the golden chains dissolved into motes of paradoxical light.
His form reconstituted itself silently, authority and motion returning in layers as if rewound by unseen hands.
The air was heavy, but his posture remained unshaken.
Across from him, Moiraine remained statuesque.
Her expression, while unchanging in its celestial poise, held the imperceptible trace of tension, a single fracture beneath the grandeur.
Her tone carried the weight of an edict rather than apology.
"My apologies for the earlier action," she said, her voice a calm wonder of existence.
"It was a breach of decorum.
But what we witnessed was something that could only lead to that reaction."
Noah regarded her with quiet thought as his wounds slowly healed "And what anomaly would compel you to act in such a manner?"
Moiraine’s gaze, like a pair of Wheels rotating in silence, turned to him fully.
"The emergence of a Living Paradox like yourself without the taint of Inevitability when coming in contact with another Paradox... should not be possible."
She spoke with solemn deliberation as her gorgeous figure had waves of glorious light of paradox bouncing over her like an endless invisible sea.
"Throughout the Ages, Living Paradoxes have not been able to reproduce.
When we resonate with each other, Inevitabilities arise- abominations born of the First Sin.
We can bond and reproduce with other Living Existences, but the act itself stirs hatred, even war.
Many conflicts occur whenever any Living Paradox touches any Living Existence."
She shifted ever so slightly, an infinitesimal movement that carried existential meaning.
"As other Existences multiplied and endured over the eons, we can only wait.
Wait for Young Paradoxes to emerge naturally throughout the Folds since paradox is always present.
But that process has slowed to a trickle.
To the point that as I mentioned before...Unbound Living Paradoxes are now rare!
And you..."
A beat of silence passed.
"You resonated with me, and yet nothing rose.
No Inevitability.
That changes many things.
That changes Everything."
HUUM!
Noah’s inner vision shimmered.
|The Living True Source of the Protagonist shakes its head with incredulity, as such an entanglement and progression is not something even it imagined.|
|The Living True Source of Paradox stares at the Living True Source of Origin.|
His True Sources looked at each other.
His weavings buzzed!
Noah said nothing aloud.
But his thoughts churned with silent depth.
He was paradoxical, yes.
But he was also a Living Origin.
The Living Protagonist, the Living Infinity, the Living Singed...and more!
He could also become a Living Quantum, and many more!
A Living Existence layered in contradiction and unity, wielding resonance without birthing chaos.
Something that should not be.
But was.
He looked at Moiraine.
Her bearing was calm, measured as always.
Regal beyond emotion.
She had not raised her voice.
She had not broken her poise.
But within her words, within her measured cadence, he could feel the hesitation and disbelief.
She did not know what he was.
And she would not truly know.
Not yet.
Not ever.
Not until he decided on his own terms what she and many others would come to know!
For now, there was simply navigating this shocking progression.

chapters.title: Chapter 3827: What are you?! II
paragraphs: A silence, deep and vast, hung in the air like a pause between breaths. And then, Oryzarakh returned.
His form- black gold, towering, monolithic- emerged from the depths of Folded space with terrifying finality. Pressure surged with his arrival, reality groaning in reverence.
"Everything is ready," he stated, each word dropping like hammers of existence.
Moiraine turned toward him, her golden white robe flowing like liquid paradox. Her gaze, ancient and piercing, returned to Noah.

"We may be at the precipice of something potentially grand," she said, solemnly. "I will verify it one last time. And for the chains, consider that debt owed. Just once more, let me see your Paradox."
She raised her hand, calm and graceful, her fingertips igniting with a white-gold glow. Paradox unfurled like a symphony.
Noah watched silently.
He lifted his own hand. It too was painted with the hues of Paradox- the Living True Source swirling like a patient serpent.
As their palms drew close, the air between them warped.
Black and gold met. Authority mixed. Not repelled. Not resisted. But harmonized.

|Your authority of the Living True Source of Paradox is coming in contact with an extremely complex and pure Paradoxical Authority, studying its structure and composition as it begins to rapidly rise in complexity and purity itself.|
The fusion didn’t spark ruin. It birthed potential. An intricate spiral of black-gold weavings spun in the air like a blooming flower of infinite regress and possibilities!
Noah’s mind was already dissecting the event as he also confirmed it!
Moiraine’s eyes remained locked onto his, and for the first time, there was no calmness in her face. Only a slight sense of awe, hesitation, and conflicted wonder.

"There isn’t time to fully explain the true extent of what this means," she said, her voice low. "But understand this. You are the first Living Paradox whose resonance with other Living Paradoxes has not spawned an Inevitability. That alone makes you an unknown and in a level of danger you cannot imagine. We must go."
WAA!
Noah’s golden eyes gleamed.
"Go where, exactly?" he asked.
Moiraine turned, gesturing to the void above. Her voice became heavy.

"To the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds. Where Foldless Ones reign. Where Wonders are forged, and where Wheels of Existence that have survived their Breakings reign. We have to be there because from this moment on, any title you once carried means nothing. You are now an enemy to the rest of the Living Existences moreso than any common Living Paradox. Oryzarakh..."
Oryzarakh’s voice came cold and absolute as he stared at Noah closely while replying, "Hold on, one more must come. I will not leave him behind."
He closed his eyes. A ripple of pressure rolled through the Folded air. Space compressed, then snapped.
BOOM!
An eruption of energy announced the arrival of a being whose appearance crackled with quiet significance.
Silver hair. Crimson eyes. White robe stitched with paradox.
It was...Aetheron.
His crimson eyes were languid and filled with power as he looked around, eventually coming to lock onto Noah!
Noah met his gaze and nearly laughed aloud.
The causal chain of events- instigated by this elegant bastard- had somehow placed both of them here.
He would not forget. Nor would he fault him as Noah was thr one to release the terrifying weavings of the Protagonist!
Aetheron looked around, his brows furrowed. "What is this? What is happening?"
Oryzarakh didn’t offer explanation. He simply stated, "Plans have changed. We have to go now."
The urgency in his tone conveyed necessity.
Moiraine floated closer to Noah, her steps made of paradox, her body radiating pure Complexity.
She surveyed the surroundings with narrowed eyes, like one awaiting a storm.
Noah took everything in and tilted his head. "How exactly does one enter the so called Transcendent Paradoxical Folds?"
Moiraine tapped a single finger to the air. Her tone was calm. "Through a Transcendent Foldpath. Hold still."
Then...Existence split open.
A beam of black-gold light erupted from the void above, immense and absolute.
It slammed down around them like a column forged from the spine of Existence.
Within it, lattices burned.
Tens of millions of Existential Dimensional Lattices forged from runes that bore names older than time spun with maddening order.
The beam cocooned them in a heavy Paradoxical authority. Noah felt his very Existence being unraveled and reconstructed, and yet at the same time not!
Moiraine was close. Her hand pressed gently onto his shoulder, her eyes never once leaving the horizons beyond. She remained alert, prepared for anything.
And Noah continued to observed everything!
Every lattice. Every folding equation of the Foldpath. Every prompt that flickered across his perception.
He reflected on all that was currently happening.

He saw how his refusal to amalgamate any single True Source early on, his choice to delay this evolution until he had a Living Wheel of Existence, how the emergence of the Living True Sources...how every step led here!
Noah smiled calmly.
Tyranny. Quintessence. Paradox. Origin.
He had not yet begun to fully wield them, and still, he had brought the Foldless Ones to him.
Entities that even Primarchs of the Chronosect treated with fear.
Now, Moiraine hovered at his side, unknowingly aiding the rise of an entity beyond their framework.
As of this moment...he would see it through. He would climb this mountain to its impossible peak.
The Foldless Ones had ruled long before his time.
Now, he would see how they did it, and where!
HUUM!

With a blinding flash of light, the four of them disappeared as their figures were pulled by the blinding brilliance of the Transcendent Foldpath- being taken to a place where when a Wheel of Existence succeeded in a Transformation would emerge into!
The Paradoxical Prison of these Nullvein Gravewake Folds became unfathomably silent.
But silence...never truly remained so.
From the depths of the black sea.
Just 100 miles in, there was an obsidian coffin that had been still like all others.
Until now.
SKAA!
A horrid screech echoed out as it was none other than the screech of...an Inevitability!
Inevitabilities.
They were unique things that violated the very standing and regulations of existence as many times, things considered impossible could viably happen through them
Like the impossibility of hiding from two Foldless Ones!
Or thr impossibility of escaping a Paradoxical Prison once...and returning into it again.
At this moment, the obsidian coffin at the bottom of this sea opened to reveal a mass of colored tentacles that a single entity stepped out of as he breathed haggardly!
This entity pulsed with waves of Finality as he gasped for breath.
"I thought I was dead for sure before those fucking monsters of existence...but what did I just see? Just what did you show me, my dear Osmont!"
Thauron, the Null Monarch, smiled as he had just heard many things.
Things that he could do use to open up many paths!
He strokes the Inevitability as he crawled out of the coffin with no grace, whispering softly to himself.
"Oh Little Bobby, I wish you were cognizant enough to witness all that would unfold!"
Finality surged.
Inevitability screeched.
And just like in the very beginnings of the Earliest Folds, something...hungered!

chapters.title: Chapter 3828: Journey Into The Unknown! I
paragraphs: The waters of the black sea stirred.

A slow humming echoed through the Paradoxical Prison- a tune without melody, drifting on no wind. The surface broke as a figure emerged, slick with shadow and humming louder, as if expecting an audience.

"I know you can’t answer me as you feed the Inevitability, Little Bobby," Thauron whispered, voice amused, chin lifting as water slid from his shoulders. "But one has to always be careful when things seem too good to be true... did they really leave this prison all alone? Without a Warden? A prison full of Primarchs and Masters of Existence who absolutely hate Foldless Ones?"
His voice wasn’t loud. It didn’t need to be. His presence alone rippled through the coils of paradox.

Thauron rose fully from the obsidian tides, tall and robed in frayed dark silk laced with ruinous markings. The tentacles of the Inevitability slithered lazily behind him, dripping with corruption, as if they too listened to the tune.
He laughed.
Low, disbelieving. Almost impressed.
"I’m not dead," he said softly, eyes scanning the hollow sky where the Warden’s presence should have pressed down like weight. "This prison was truly left empty."
His hand raised, glowing with a flickering light drawn from the True Source of Finality. The power surged in quiet pulses across his skin.
"So here we are, Little Bobby," he said, turning slowly as he took in the thousands of black coffins floating in endless chains. "A place filled with meals, locked in boxes."
He chuckled again.

"One has to eat slowly, of course. But what can one achieve if they swallow everything in this prison? If they pair it with the secret that caused two Foldless Ones to rush out in such haste... can I actually make something of myself, Little Bobby?"
His eyes gleamed.
They didn’t shine like stars. They burned like the fading embers of ancient furnaces that had long since turned to ash.
He turned his gaze downward.
"First, I would have to find other Living Existences."
He clicked his tongue, his grin widening.
"But that alone is difficult. All these folds nearby are ruled by Living Paradoxes. Not many Living Origins just floating around. Nor Living Spirits. Nor Living Elementals."
His feet lifted, body gliding lazily into the air. The Inevitability rose beside him like a faithful shadow.
"Difficult, Little Bobby. The path ahead is difficult," he said, voice quiet. "But something difficult is something worth having. I will start with the prison first."
The laughter of the Inevitability screeched behind him. A howl of hunger.
Far from the Paradoxical Prison, far from the dark coils of Thauron and his muttering, another movement stirred.
In the Nullvein Gravewake Folds, beyond the border that tethered the Paradoxical Prison.
It was the Veiled Sunfolds.
Nestled beneath shadow, under the endless dusk of the Nullvein’s curvature, the Veiled Sunfolds burned with a quiet, unnatural golden light.
And there, hidden in the crook of lightless space, the cross-shaped Living Origin Labyrinth opened once more.
The Labyrinth pulsed with structured runes of the Origin. Its halls branched endlessly, carved not from stone but from the threads of reality- crossing space, memory, and time.
Near the entrance, Master Hannibal arrived once again. His face cloaked. His eyes narrow.

Trailing behind him, veiled in suppressing Existential Dimensional Lattices, were forces from the Mannafolds and from the Chronosect of the Threadbound Folds. They moved like whispers, like regrets sliding along the edge of thought. They slipped inside. Undetected.
The few Masters of Existence that had come to surround this place did not sense anything wrong occurring!
Within the Labyrinth itself.
Inside the folds of the Labyrinth’s deepest chambers, far beyond where ordinary explorers could reach, two Living Origin Descendants stood in quiet debate.
The male was tall and thoughtful, his skin faintly etched with the burn of pure weaving.
His companion, the female, tilted her head curiously as her eyes narrowed at the slowly dimming illusory screen showing Noah’s defeat of the Imitation Mutated Inevitability.
Beside them, a fairy-like creature floated with wings of Origin light as it was the Guider.
"These Fold Dwellers," the woman said, her voice rich and curious. "They come from regions watched over by Living Paradoxes, yes?"
The male sighed.
"Yes," he said, affirming it again.
She gestured toward the fading image.
"And yet, before even starting the path of Origin properly, they defeated an Inevitability?"
He remained quiet.
She smiled then. Something bright and hungry.
"I want to know more."
The man shook his head.

"Dealing with Living Paradoxes is never an easy affair," he said. "And lately... the Core Origin Descendants from the Origin Folds have warned that something is shifting. The Paradoxes are growing restless. Something’s changed."
She waved a hand, dismissing.
"Warnings are warnings. Will you really ignore this? A Fold Dweller, not even a Master of Existence, barely initiated, defeating an Inevitability? Don’t you want to investigate?"
He did not answer at first.
She leaned forward, coaxing.
He closed his eyes.
"I will extend my weavings through the region they entered," he said finally. "I will see what Paradoxical presence watches over their folds. Then I will decide."
She clapped her hands.
"Do it, do it!"
He brought his hand out.
The fairy-like creature drifted downward, its glow intensifying. It settled in his palm.
He closed his fingers around it. He inhaled.
And his existence rippled.
Complex weavings stretched from him like ghost-light, disappearing into the unseen fabrics that stretched across Folds.
Silence.
Then, a breath later, his eyes snapped open. A frown etched across his face.
"What is it?" she asked.
His voice was quiet.
"I...do not sense a present influence of a Living Paradox," he said.
She blinked.
"You mean the Folds these Fold Dwellers come from...aren’t being watched?"
Such a thing would be ridiculous, right?
He nodded slowly.
"Not by a Paradox. Not now."
The fairy pulsed once, as if confused.
"That," the woman whispered, her voice touched with wonder, "is interesting."
Her smile widened.
"Shall we see why a Fold of Paradoxes is empty?"
A daring idea. One that this time...was not denied!
A Fold devoid of the piercing eyes of its owner.
A Prison devoid of the piercing eyes of its owner!
It may have been momentarily. It may have been coincidentally.
But surely, nothing too grand would come out of this, right?
Right?!

They moved like whispers, like regrets sliding along the edge of thought.
They slipped inside.
Undetected.
The few Masters of Existence that had come to surround this place did not sense anything wrong occurring!
Within the Labyrinth itself.
Inside the folds of the Labyrinth’s deepest chambers, far beyond where ordinary explorers could reach, two Living Origin Descendants stood in quiet debate.
The male was tall and thoughtful, his skin faintly etched with the burn of pure weaving.
His companion, the female, tilted her head curiously as her eyes narrowed at the slowly dimming illusory screen showing Noah’s defeat of the Imitation Mutated Inevitability.
Beside them, a fairy-like creature floated with wings of Origin light as it was the Guider.
"These Fold Dwellers," the woman said, her voice rich and curious.
"They come from regions watched over by Living Paradoxes, yes?"
The male sighed.
"Yes," he said, affirming it again.
She gestured toward the fading image.
"And yet, before even starting the path of Origin properly, they defeated an Inevitability?"
He remained quiet.
She smiled then.
Something bright and hungry.
"I want to know more."
The man shook his head.
"Dealing with Living Paradoxes is never an easy affair," he said.
"And lately... the Core Origin Descendants from the Origin Folds have warned that something is shifting.
The Paradoxes are growing restless.
Something’s changed."
She waved a hand, dismissing.
"Warnings are warnings.
Will you really ignore this?
A Fold Dweller, not even a Master of Existence, barely initiated, defeating an Inevitability?
Don’t you want to investigate?"
He did not answer at first.
She leaned forward, coaxing.
He closed his eyes.
"I will extend my weavings through the region they entered," he said finally.
"I will see what Paradoxical presence watches over their folds.
Then I will decide."
She clapped her hands.
"Do it, do it!"
He brought his hand out.
The fairy-like creature drifted downward, its glow intensifying.
It settled in his palm.
He closed his fingers around it.
He inhaled.
And his existence rippled.
Complex weavings stretched from him like ghost-light, disappearing into the unseen fabrics that stretched across Folds.
Silence.
Then, a breath later, his eyes snapped open.
A frown etched across his face.
"What is it?" she asked.
His voice was quiet.
"I...do not sense a present influence of a Living Paradox," he said.
She blinked.
"You mean the Folds these Fold Dwellers come from...aren’t being watched?"
Such a thing would be ridiculous, right?
He nodded slowly.
"Not by a Paradox.
Not now."
The fairy pulsed once, as if confused.
"That," the woman whispered, her voice touched with wonder, "is interesting."
Her smile widened.
"Shall we see why a Fold of Paradoxes is empty?"
A daring idea.
One that this time...was not denied!
A Fold devoid of the piercing eyes of its owner.
A Prison devoid of the piercing eyes of its owner!
It may have been momentarily.
It may have been coincidentally.
But surely, nothing too grand would come out of this, right?
Right?!

chapters.title: Chapter 3829: Journey Into The Unknown! II
paragraphs: In the crucible that was forging the future of an entire Infiniverse, Noah stood still.
His body pulsed with power, arms raised slightly as both hands glowed with quiet pressure.

Before him, the True Source of Gravitation surged forth- thousands of Lattices, lined in spirals, their force tangible. The space around Noah warped subtly, drawing Ruination and the Infiniverse Body forward from their distant positions.
No matter how much their Lattices fought back, his sheer collection of percentage Resistance was too high!
Their forms hovered gently, unable to resist the calling of their master’s gravitational will.

Ruination’s dark crimson-gold figure shimmered as she floated into place while continuing to struggle. The Infiniverse Body followed, her luminous white gold form laced with fractal frequencies humming faintly.
Two items slowly manifested in front of them.
10x Living True Source Panaceas and 10x Primarchical Pearls of the True Source of Sacrifice!
Noah’s expression was calm.
He looked to Ruination, his eyes holding the trace of a smile. "Can you multiply these for me?" he asked, the tone light, but the weight unmistakable.
He had asked something similar not too long ago!
Ruination’s gaze tightened. She remembered the last time she said no as...her answer came without delay.
"Master...let me try first."
Her hands, painted in crimson and gold, reached forward.
The ten Panaceas and ten Primarchical Pearls floated into her grasp as her expression became stern. As if she had to do whatever it would take to allow some form of multiplication to succeed!
Behind her, the illusion of a vast crimson Wheel spun into being. Its shape was clearer than before. A Wheel of Ruination, comprised of multiple True Frequencies orbiting a stable singularity.
Dozens. Hundreds. The Frequencies of Ruination glowed and flared, matching her pulse. Power radiated outward like waves from a struck bell.
She clutched the Loot tightly as from Ruin itself, she wanted to produce wonder.
For her Master. For herself.
And so...she burned all the Existential Dimensional Lattices she held in her banner for this purpose as massive crimson runes began to swirl around her!
A low hum began.
Then...
BOOM.
A silent burst of brilliance.
Light cracked in the Crucible from one end to the other as if the very laws of balance had bent to obey her will. The two types of Loot, so rare and invaluable, multiplied by 2 before Noah’s eyes.
He smiled, the corners of his mouth tugging upward slightly. "Excellent."
He beckoned and gazed at the wondrous loot before he separated the spoils evenly. Ten of the Panaceas for Ruination for the Infiniverse Body.
The 20 Primarchical Pearls of the True Source of Sacrifice could be given to his people to produce 20 Primarchs of Existence!
He nodded to himself as he spoke.
"I need both of you closer to Originus Venerant as soon as possible," he said,"The next stages will not be forgiving."
WAA!
Ruination nodded with fervent eyes.
The Infiniverse Body bowed slightly, acknowledging his intent.
Noah then turned his eyes to her, tone shifting to something more contemplative.

"We now know that the Wheels of Existence that are successful in their Transformation are elevated to the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds...and likely other Transcendent Folds. As of this moment, we can assume an endless variation of Folds. Origin Folds, Elemental Folds, Temporal Folds...But for now, we worry about our own Wheel. Yours. Ruination’s. And my Atlas..."
HUUM!
He let the idea hang in the air.
"How quickly can the Infiniverse Wheel of Existence undertake the transformation?"
The Infiniverse Body closed her eyes. Layers of data rotated behind her eyelids like transparent scripts of stars. When she opened them again, she spoke simply.
"Ninety-nine percent chance of success- if the transformation is initiated after attaining Originus Venerant."
Noah’s eyes lit up.
He turned to both of them.
"My body of Ozymandias will soon reach the new location. What waits there is filled with questions...and many answers. Pay attention. What I learns, you will soon need to understand."
Ruination and the Infiniverse Body nodded in tandem.
"Then let’s get back to it."
BZZT!
He raised his arms again.
From his spine, thousands of golden Lattices of Kuklos bloomed outwards.
A golden Wheel behind him manifested and glowed brighter, heavier. Its pressure spread through the Crucible, shaping all things!
The Forging of the Infiniverse Crucible...continued.
Far away, in another stretch of Existence, Noah’s body of Ozymandias traveled.
The Transcendent Foldpath stretched up before him, a winding path across existence that twisted and split like a living roadmap.
Trillions of Event Horizons flickered across their path- shifting thresholds that acted as doors between truths and falsities.
Event horizons were like the edge of perception. They marked the point where one could no longer return to what they knew.
One...could no longer return.
That was how it was supposed to be, anyways.
Cross one Event Horizon, and the laws changed. Memories shifted. Existence bent.
They crossed them again and again.
Moiraine and Oryzarakh floated ahead in silence, their bodies still like old statues- but minds clearly active. Their light glinted softly each time a new horizon passed.
Behind them, Aetheron watched Noah as the both of them were carried and protected by their pull.
His silver hair fell messily over his crimson eyes, and his smile barely masked the tension underneath.
"You," he finally said, his voice thick with laziness and suspicion. "What did you do?"
Noah’s face turned toward him slowly as he spoke.
"We haven’t been officially introduced," he said. "You were waiting for me in the Hollow Concord of Nullity, weren’t you?"
He smiled faintly.
"I regret missing that meeting. I imagine it would’ve been a...tasty encounter."
Aetheron’s smile sharpened.
Just before he could reply, Moiraine’s voice rang out.
"Enough."
She didn’t shout. She merely spoke.
But both beings listened.
"No hostilities," she said. "If you wish to live long in the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds and have a good time, drop any hostility towards him now."
Aetheron smiled towards Noah and looked amused, almost as if he was goading him and letting him know his place.
But the words of Moiraine continued.
"I was talking to you, abomination."
BOOM!
Moiraine said while looking at him directly, his gaze changing.
"I’m telling you to behave. Because if this unfolds as I believe it will...this Young Paradox will outrank you in every sense. Having any hostilities towards him will not benefit you at all."
Aetheron: "..."
Her tone held no room for disagreement.
She added, "Your father protects you. That’s all."
Aetheron’s gaze darkened.
He said nothing.
Then he looked away, his face turning full of suspicion!
"...So what happened?" he asked again. "What changed everything?"
Moiraine and Oryzarakh exchanged no glances. For a moment, they gave no answer.
But finally, Moiraine spoke.
"A Sin might actually stand a possibility of being reversed," she said.
"A Sin from the Earliest Folds. One that could never have been reversed before."
She did not say everything clearly.
The silence that followed was deep.
Noah took in her words quietly, weighing the scale of what flowed in her mind while he planned for all possibilities.
In the next moment, Moiraine’s hand on his shoulder tightened slightly.
"We are arriving."
